To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

high dimensional registration techniques can improve the sensitivity of functional data analysis in regions of high anatomical variability, such as auditory cortex and the surrounding superior temporal region, when compared to conventional normalization techniques.

(1) HAMMER is superior to DARTEL in terms of fSNR, (2) HAMMER and DARTEL are superior to cosine basis functions and unified segmentation in terms of fMRI activation in auditory regions, (3) HAMMER results in more localized fMRI activations in the auditory cortex than DARTEL or the low dimensional normalization techniques, and (4) spatial smoothing improves fMRI sensitivity, but also increases the size of activation foci.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to best align anatomical images for fMRI group analysis.
improving functional data analysis by reducing inter subject anatomical variations.
the problem of inter subject anatomically variability in fMRI data, and how this can affect the analysis of functional data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a high dimensional registration (HAMMER) in conjunction with a high resolution template image is a better approach for normalization of fMRI data in this region of the brain.
HAMMER, DARTEL, and the cosine basis function method in SPM are all better than unified segmentation for fMRI analysis, but that HAMMER and DARTEL are superior to the other methods.

the use of high dimensional registration techniques such as HAMMER can be recommended for the study of auditory cortex and other regions of the superior temporal lobe, where inter subject anatomical variations are large, and spatial resolution is important.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the high dimensional technique is able to preserve the anatomical information in the single subject template, while the other techniques tend to smooth away the anatomical information and blur the functional activation.
the high dimensional registration technique HAMMER is able to capitalize on high resolution anatomical information from a single subject to improve functional data analysis.

the use of high dimensional anatomical registration techniques, such as HAMMER or DARTEL, can improve fMRI data analysis, especially for regions with high anatomical variability, such as auditory cortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

high dimensional normalization can be used to reduce the effect of inter subject anatomically variability, and thus, can be used to enhance fMRI analysis, especially when the goal is to localize activation to subregions of auditory and superior temporal cortex.

, when using a single subject template, the HAMMER technique can improve fSNR in the superior temporal region and in the region of the auditory cortex, with the advantage of retaining spatial localization of activation.
the choice of registration method is critical to the success of fMRI data analysis.
